# pm-facing_alias: # Schema: PM-facing alias, wire-format model id, reasoning effort.
# This file is the codex adapter alias table. The claude adapter alias table
# lives at share/claude-model-aliases.tsv (same 3-column format); the opencode
# one lives at share/opencode-model-aliases.tsv.
# Columns must be tab-separated.
# Executor-agnostic alias — use in briefs, PM routing, and dispatch policy docs:
#   `light`  — lightweight/fast model for targeted changes (< 50 lines, ≤ 2 files,
#              no new behavioral units). Mapped per executor:
#                codex  → luna        (gpt-6-luna)
#                claude → haiku       (claude-haiku-5-5, see claude-model-aliases.tsv)
# The codex CLI lists its models with `codex debug models` (checked against
#   gpt-6.1-sol    — latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work
#   gpt-6-astra    — frontier intelligence for the most demanding work
#   gpt-6-sol      — previous-generation workhorse
#   gpt-6-luna     — fast and affordable model for easier tasks
#   gpt-5.6-sol / gpt-5.6-terra / gpt-5.6-luna — older generation, still listed
# Default model: pm-dispatch pins its OWN default model (gpt-6.1-sol, see
# DEFAULT_DISPATCH_MODEL in adapters/codex/dispatch.sh), decoupled from the
# user's interactive ~/.codex/config.toml `model` setting. Omitting --model
# therefore dispatches on gpt-6.1-sol — NOT whatever the local codex config
# defaults to. Override per-host via ~/.pm-dispatch/config `dispatch.default_model`.
#   gpt-6.1-sol    — primary default (workhorse tier)
#   gpt-6-sol      — fallback (set dispatch.default_model = gpt-6-sol if gpt-6.1-sol is unavailable)
#   gpt-5.6-terra  — second fallback (the previous default, balanced tier)
# `gpt-6-astra` (frontier) and `gpt-6-luna` (fast/affordable) are available as
# explicit aliases for callers who want to name a tier directly — neither is
# the default; see docs/model-tier-policy.md for when to reach for the
# frontier tier.
# `gpt-5.5` / `gpt-5.4` are no longer listed by the codex CLI; they stay as
# aliases so an older `dispatch.default_model` still resolves with the same
# effort, and fail with the CLI's own error if the model is gone.
# `codex-spark` names gpt-5.3-codex-spark explicitly (an independent usage pool,
# ~64K ctx); it is not listed by the CLI above, is opt-in only and is no longer
# what `light` means.
# Context window reference:
#   light / gpt-6-luna    — see `codex debug models` for the current window
#   codex-spark           — gpt-5.3-codex-spark  ~64K tokens
# Survey-style briefs that read large files MUST use lazy-read instructions.
# Reasoning effort: an alias's effort column is the practical default whenever
# `--effort` is omitted (it takes precedence over the global default — see
# runtime/lib/reasoning-effort.sh). default and every gpt-* alias converge to
# medium so a plain dispatch/gate call is medium by default without needing
# `--effort medium` on every invocation; codex-spark stays high, unchanged and
# orthogonal to this convergence (its small-model/low-latency tuning is a
# separate concern from reasoning depth).
default
gpt-6.1-sol
gpt-6-sol
astra
gpt-6-astra
luna
gpt-6-luna
light
gpt-5.6-terra
gpt-5.6-sol
gpt-5.6-luna
gpt-5.5
gpt-5.4
codex-spark
